name: Ability Capsule
description: A capsule that allows a Pokémon with two standard Abilities to switch between those Abilities when used.
notes: Cannot switch to or from Hidden Abilities; fails with Fling when held.

name: Ability Patch
description: A patch that changes a Pokémon’s Ability to its Hidden Ability.
notes: In Generation IX, it can also remove a Hidden Ability and revert to the first Ability slot.

name: Ability Shield
description: A held item that protects the holder from having its Ability changed, suppressed, or ignored.

name: Ability Urge
description: A Wonder Launcher-exclusive battle item that activates the Ability of an ally Pokémon. Only works with Abilities that activate upon entering battle.
notes: Wonder Launcher exclusive. Costs 3 points to use. Works with: Anticipation, Download, Drizzle, Drought, Forecast, Forewarn, Frisk, Intimidate, Sand Stream, Slow Start, Snow Warning, and Trace.

name: Abomasite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Abomasnow to Mega Evolve into Mega Abomasnow when held.

name: Abra Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Abra, Kadabra, or Alakazam.

name: Absolite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Absol to Mega Evolve into Mega Absol when held.

name: Absolite Z
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Absol to Mega Evolve into Mega Absol Z during battle.

name: Absorb Bulb
description: A consumable bulb that raises the holder's Special Attack by one stage when hit by a damaging Water-type move.

name: Academy Ball
description: A standard-issue academy ball that can be brought out during a picnic and kicked around by the player and their Pokémon.

name: Academy Bottle
description: A decorative picnic item emblazoned with the academy's emblem.

name: Academy Chairs
description: A set of chairs used to decorate the player's picnic.

name: Academy Cup
description: A standard-issue academy cup used to decorate the player's picnic.

name: Academy Tablecloth
description: A standard-issue academy tablecloth used to decorate the player's picnic.
notes: Having this item allows a picnicker on Reveler's Road in front of Kitakami Hall to give the player the Academy Chairs.

name: Acro Bike
description: A folding bicycle that allows the rider to perform tricks such as wheelies and bunny hops to reach special areas.
notes: Counterpart to the Mach Bike.

name: Adamant Crystal
description: A large, glowing gem associated with Dialga that allows it to change form and boosts its power.
notes: Associated with the Pokémon of myth Dialga; categorized as a Key Item in Generation VIII and as an Other Item in Generation IX.

name: Adamant Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to Adamant, boosting Attack while lowering Special Attack.

name: Adamant Orb
description: A brightly gleaming orb associated with Dialga that boosts the power of its Dragon- and Steel-type moves when held.
notes: Required to encounter Dialga at Spear Pillar in Pokémon Platinum.

name: Adrenaline Orb
description: A consumable item that boosts a Pokémon’s Speed when intimidated or increases wild Pokémon calling for help in battle.

name: Adventure Guide
description: A key item that lets the player review basic gameplay information and tutorials encountered during the adventure.
notes: Known as Adventure Rules prior to Pokémon Sword and Shield.

name: Aerodactyl Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Aerodactyl.

name: Aerodactylite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Aerodactyl to Mega Evolve into Mega Aerodactyl.

name: Aggronite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Aggron to Mega Evolve into Mega Aggron.

name: Aguav Berry
description: A Berry that restores HP when a Pokémon is in a pinch but may cause confusion if the Pokémon dislikes bitter flavors.

name: Aipom Hair
description: A material dropped by Aipom or Ambipom that can be exchanged for LP or used with the Item Printer.
notes: Not used in any TM recipes

name: Air Balloon
description: A held item that makes the holder float above the ground until it is hit, at which point it bursts.

name: Air Mail
description: Stationery featuring a print of colorful letter sets that a Pokémon can hold to deliver a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation IV games.

name: Alakazite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Alakazam to Mega Evolve into Mega Alakazam.

name: Alomomola Mucus
description: A material dropped by Alomomola that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Aloraichium Z
description: A Pokémon-specific Z-Crystal that allows Alolan Raichu to upgrade Thunderbolt into the Z-Move Stoked Sparksurfer.
notes: Pokémon-specific Z-Crystal associated with Alolan Raichu.

name: Altarianite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Altaria to Mega Evolve into Mega Altaria when held.

name: Amaze Mulch
description: A fertilizer used in Berry fields that can increase harvest yield, promote Berry mutations, and affect soil drying.

name: Amazing Butter
description: A pack of butter used by Ansha to make higher-quality donuts, allowing the use of up to six berries.

name: Ampharosite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Ampharos to Mega Evolve into Mega Ampharos.

name: Amulet Coin
description: A held item that doubles the prize money earned after battles when the holder participates.
notes: Does not stack with Luck Incense or other Amulet Coins.

name: Antidote
description: A spray-type medicine that cures a Pokémon of poisoning.

name: Apicot Berry
description: A Berry that raises the holder’s Special Defense when its HP is low.

name: Apple
description: A very sweet ingredient sliced thin and used for making sandwiches.

name: Applin Juice
description: A material dropped by Applin and its evolutions that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Apricorn
description: A fruit used as a crafting material to create various types of Poké Balls.
notes: Also known as the Brown Apricorn.

name: Apricorn Box
description: A handy box that allows the player to store and manage Apricorns.

name: Aqua Suit
description: A technologically advanced suit developed by Team Aqua that can withstand any impact.

name: Arboliva Oil
description: A special oil produced by Paldea's Arboliva, treasured for its exquisite taste and used in cooking.
notes: Introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

name: Armor Fossil
description: A fossil that can be regenerated into Shieldon.
notes: Counterpart of the Skull Fossil.

name: Armor Pass
description: A pass that allows the player to travel to the Isle of Armor by showing it to the rail staff at Wedgehurst Station.

name: Armorite Ore
description: Rare ore found on the Isle of Armor that can be exchanged with collectors for various benefits.

name: Arrokuda Scales
description: A material dropped by Arrokuda or Barraskewda that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Articuno Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Articuno.

name: Articuno Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Articuno.
notes: Used to encounter Articuno in Paldea by showing it to Snacksworth.

name: Aspear Berry
description: A Berry that cures a Pokémon of being frozen when used or held.
notes: Spiritual successor to the Burnt Berry; Natural Gift type is Ice.

name: Assault Vest
description: A held item that boosts the holder’s Special Defense but prevents the use of status moves.

name: Audinite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Audino to Mega Evolve into Mega Audino when held.

name: Aurora Ticket
description: An event ticket that allows access to Birth Island, where Deoxys can be encountered.

name: Auspicious Armor
description: A peculiar set of armor that can make a certain species of Pokémon evolve.

name: Autograph
description: An autograph given by Vermilion City Gym Leader Lt. Surge as a commemorative keepsake.

name: Autographed Plush
description: A plush doll that has been autographed by Canari. Just having one puts you in a good mood.

name: Aux Evasion
description: A battle item that temporarily makes moves less likely to strike the targeted Pokémon.
notes: Exclusive to Pokémon Legends: Arceus

name: Aux Guard
description: A battle item that temporarily boosts a Pokémon’s defensive stats.
notes: Exclusive to Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

name: Aux Power
description: A battle item that sharply boosts a Pokémon’s offensive stats during battle until it leaves the field.
notes: Exclusive to Pokémon Legends: Arceus

name: Aux Powerguard
description: A battle item that sharply boosts a Pokémon’s offensive and defensive stats during battle until it leaves the field.
notes: Exclusive to Pokémon Legends: Arceus

name: Avocado
description: A mild-tasting but rich ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: Awakening
description: A spray-type medicine that wakes a Pokémon from sleep or drowsiness.

name: Axew Scales
description: A material dropped by the Axew evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Azelf's Fang
description: Proof of completing Azelf's trial at Lake Valor, required to forge the Red Chain.

name: Azure Flute
description: A mysterious flute that emits otherworldly echoes and is used to access the Hall of Origin where Arceus resides.
notes: Event item in Generation IV that was never distributed; obtainable normally in Pokémon Legends: Arceus and as a save data bonus in Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl.

name: Azurill Fur
description: A material dropped by Azurill, Marill, or Azumarill that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Babiri Berry
description: A Berry that reduces the damage taken from a super effective Steel-type attack when held.

name: Bach's Food Tin
description: An ingredient that can be used for cooking curry at camp, consisting of tinned food sold by Bach.

name: Bacon
description: A very salty cooked ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: Bag
description: A vital tool that stores all of the player's items, allowing them to be used, arranged, or discarded.

name: Bagon Scales
description: A material dropped by the Bagon evolutionary line that can be exchanged for LP or used with the Item Printer.
notes: Not used in any TM recipes

name: Baguette
description: A type of sandwich ingredient with a straightforward, salty wheat flavor that pairs well with many fillings.
notes: Currently unobtainable.

name: Ball of Mud
description: A hardened ball of mud that can be thrown to stun Pokémon and is used as a crafting material.

name: Balm Mushroom
description: A rare, fragrant mushroom that serves no purpose other than being sold for a high price.
notes: Formatted as BalmMushroom prior to Generation VI.

name: Banana
description: A very sweet ingredient used for making sandwiches.

name: Band Autograph
description: An unused Key Item signed by all members of Galar’s most charismatic band, the Maximizers.
notes: Unused and unobtainable in normal gameplay.

name: Banettite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Banette to Mega Evolve into Mega Banette when held.

name: Barbaracite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Barbaracle to Mega Evolve into Mega Barbaracle during battle.

name: Barboach Slime
description: A material dropped by Barboach or Whiscash that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Barred Cup
description: A decorative cup used to embellish the player's picnic setup.

name: Basculegion Food
description: A favored food of Basculegion that allows the player to befriend it and unlock it as a Ride Pokémon.

name: Basculin Fang
description: A material dropped by Basculin or Basculegion that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Basement Key (Hoenn)
description: A key item used to unlock the door to New Mauville beneath Mauville City.
notes: Hoenn-specific Basement Key used for New Mauville.

name: Basement Key (Johto)
description: A key that opens the locked door to the basement of the Goldenrod Tunnel.
notes: Johto-specific Basement Key used in Goldenrod City.

name: Basil
description: A fragrant, bitter herb ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: Battle Chairs
description: A set of chairs designed for picnicking, inspired by the Battle Tablecloth.

name: Battle Pocket
description: Contains all items which only have effect in battle, including Mega Stones.

name: Battle Tablecloth
description: A decorative picnic tablecloth meant to inspire people and Pokémon during picnics.

name: Baxcalibrite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Baxcalibur to Mega Evolve into Mega Baxcalibur when held.
notes: Introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

name: Beach Glass
description: A piece of colored glass worn smooth by ocean waves that is valuable only for selling.

name: Bead Mail
description: A type of Mail that can be held by a Pokémon to store a written message and display a sketch of the holder.
notes: Exclusive to Generation III games.

name: Bean Cake
description: A cake made by combining beans with a Cake-Lure Base that attracts various Pokémon, especially fish and bird Pokémon.

name: Beast Ball
description: A special Poké Ball designed to catch Ultra Beasts, with a very low success rate against other Pokémon.

name: Beedrillite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Beedrill to Mega Evolve into Mega Beedrill.
notes: Unaffected by item-negating effects; cannot be traded from Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire to X and Y.

name: Beldum Claw
description: A material dropped by Beldum, Metang, or Metagross that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Bellsprout Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Bellsprout, Weepinbell, or Victreebel.

name: Bellsprout Vine
description: A material dropped by the Bellsprout evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Belue Berry
description: A very rare and extremely sour Berry primarily used as an ingredient for Pokéblocks, Poffins, and other recipes.
notes: Largest obtainable Berry; primarily an ingredient item and not directly usable.

name: Bergmite Ice
description: A material dropped by Bergmite or Avalugg that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Berry
description: A Berry exclusive to Generation II that restores 10 HP when used or consumed by a Pokémon.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II; succeeded by the Oran Berry from Generation III onward.

name: Berry Juice
description: A drink made from Berries that restores 20 HP to a Pokémon.

name: Berry Pots
description: Portable planters that allow the player to plant, water, and grow Berry trees while traveling.

name: Berry Pouch
description: A pouch that stores the Berries the player collects.

name: Berry Sweet
description: A berry-shaped sweet that can be held by Milcery to trigger its evolution into Alcremie when the player spins.

name: Berserk Gene
description: A consumable held item that sharply raises the holder’s Attack upon entering battle but causes confusion.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II core series games and heavily associated with Mewtwo.

name: Bicycle
description: A key item that allows the player to travel faster than walking or running.

name: Big Bamboo Shoot
description: A large and rare bamboo shoot that is valued primarily for selling.

name: Big Malasada
description: An Alola region local specialty that cures all non-volatile status conditions and confusion.
notes: Local specialty of the Alola region.

name: Big Mushroom
description: A large and rare mushroom that is highly valued and can be sold for a high price.
notes: More valuable version of the Tiny Mushroom.

name: Big Nugget
description: A large and valuable nugget of pure gold meant to be sold for a high price.
notes: More valuable version of the Nugget.

name: Big Pearl
description: A large, valuable pearl that is prized for its high selling price.
notes: Bigger and more valuable version of the Pearl; primarily used for selling.

name: Big Root
description: A held item that increases the amount of HP restored by HP-draining moves and effects.

name: Bike Voucher
description: A voucher that can be exchanged at the Bike Shop for a free Bicycle.

name: Binding Band
description: A held item that increases the damage inflicted by binding moves.
notes: Damage multiplier changed across generations.

name: Bitter Berry
description: A Berry that cures a Pokémon of confusion when used or held.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II; succeeded by the Persim Berry from Generation III onward.

name: Bitter Herba Mystica
description: A legendary bitter condiment used as an ingredient when making sandwiches.
notes: One of the five Herba Mystica.

name: Black Apricorn
description: A tough black fruit used to craft Heavy Balls or blend into Aprijuice.

name: Black Augurite
description: A black stone used to evolve Scyther into Kleavor.

name: Black Belt
description: A held item that boosts the power of Fighting-type moves.
notes: Formatted as Blackbelt in Generation II.

name: Black Flute
description: A flute made from black glass that alters wild Pokémon encounters when used.

name: Black Glasses
description: A pair of shady-looking glasses that boost the power of Dark-type moves when held.
notes: Formatted as BlackGlasses prior to Generation VI

name: Black Mane Hair
description: Mane hair that belonged to Spectrier, used with a Radiant Petal to create the Reins of Unity.

name: Black Sludge
description: A held item that restores HP to Poison-type Pokémon each turn but damages all other types.

name: Black Tumblestone
description: A mysterious black stone used as a crafting material to forge Heavy, Leaden, and Gigaton Balls.

name: Blank Plate
description: A stone tablet imbued with the essence of normalcy that allows a certain Pokémon to gain the power of the Normal type.
notes: Can be read; engraved with: "Three beings whose power can hold both time and space fixed."

name: Blastoisinite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Blastoise to Mega Evolve into Mega Blastoise when held.

name: Blazikenite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Blaziken to Mega Evolve into Mega Blaziken when held.
notes: Unaffected by item-negating effects; cannot be removed or transferred while held by Blaziken.

name: Blitzle Mane Hair
description: A material dropped by Blitzle or Zebstrika that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Bloom Mail
description: Stationery featuring a print of pretty floral patterns that can hold a written message when carried by a Pokémon.
notes: Exclusive to Generation IV games.

name: Blue Apricorn
description: A blue fruit used to craft Lure Balls or blend into Aprijuice.

name: Blue Bottle
description: A decorative bottle used during picnics with no practical effect beyond aesthetics.

name: Blue Canari Plush Lv. 1
description: A plush doll of Canari that slightly increases the chance of catching Pokémon.

name: Blue Canari Plush Lv. 2
description: A plush doll of Canari that increases the chance of catching Pokémon.

name: Blue Canari Plush Lv. 3
description: A plush doll of Canari that greatly increases the chance of catching Pokémon.

name: Blue Card
description: A card used to save points earned from Buena's Password radio show.

name: Blue Chairs
description: A set of chairs inspired by the Blue Tablecloth, used to decorate the player's picnic.

name: Blue Cup
description: A decorative picnic item used to customize the appearance of the player's picnic.

name: Blue Dish
description: A decorative dish used during picnics with no practical effect.
notes: Currently unobtainable.

name: Blue-Flag Pick
description: A picnic pick that flies a blue flag and is used to complete a sandwich during a picnic.

name: Blue Flute
description: A blue glass flute that awakens sleeping Pokémon.
notes: Serves no practical purpose in Generation V and Pokémon X and Y other than being sold.

name: Blue Orb
description: A legendary blue orb associated with Kyogre that can trigger its Primal Reversion.
notes: Functions as a Key Item in earlier generations and as a held item for Kyogre starting in Generation VI.

name: Blue Petal
description: A pressed flower petal collected during Mina's trial, one of seven needed to create the Rainbow Flower.

name: Blue Poké Ball Pick
description: A sandwich pick with a simple blue Poké Ball design used to complete a sandwich during a picnic.

name: Blue Scarf
description: A held item that raises the holder’s Beauty in Pokémon Contests.

name: Blue Shard
description: A small blue shard that appears to be a fragment of an ancient implement.
notes: One of the four Shards.

name: Blue-Sky Flower Pick
description: A flower pick designed to evoke a blue sky that can be used to complete a sandwich during a picnic.

name: Blue Tablecloth
description: A simple blue tablecloth used to decorate the player's picnic.
notes: Having this item allows a picnicker on Reveler's Road in front of the Kitakami Hall to give the player the Blue Chairs.

name: Blueberry Chairs
description: A set of chairs designed for picnicking, inspired by the Blueberry Tablecloth.

name: Blueberry Tablecloth
description: A picnic decoration used to customize the player's picnic table setting.
notes: Owning this item allows an NPC on Reveler's Road to give the player Blueberry Chairs.

name: Bluesky Mail
description: A type of Mail that can hold a written message and be attached to a Pokémon.
notes: Event-only item in Generation II; legitimately obtainable only via the Mobile System GB service in Japanese Pokémon Crystal.

name: Bluk Berry
description: A Berry introduced in Generation III, primarily used as an ingredient for Pokéblocks, Poffins, and other preparations.
notes: Natural Gift Fire-type; Fling power 10.

name: Blunder Policy
description: A held item that sharply raises the holder’s Speed when it misses a move due to accuracy or evasion.

name: Bob's Food Tin
description: An ingredient used for cooking curry, consisting of tinned food sold by Bob that is popular in Galar.

name: Boiled Egg
description: An ingredient that can be used for cooking, enhancing dishes even when used alone.

name: Bold Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to Bold, boosting Defense while lowering Attack.

name: Bombirdier Feather
description: A material dropped by Bombirdier that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Bonsly Tears
description: A material dropped by Bonsly or Sudowoodo that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Boost Mulch
description: A type of mulch used in Berry fields that affects how quickly soil dries.

name: Booster Energy
description: An item to be held by Pokémon with certain Abilities that activates and boosts the Pokémon's power.
notes: Consumed when activating Protosynthesis or Quark Drive but restored after battle in Scarlet and Violet.

name: Bottle Cap
description: A silver bottle cap traded to certain NPCs to maximize one of a Pokémon’s IVs through Hyper Training.
notes: The Gold Bottle Cap is a more valuable variant.

name: BoulderBadge
description: A badge item internally used like Safari bait.
notes: Index number 0x15; unobtainable.

name: Bounsweet Sweat
description: A material dropped by the Bounsweet evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Bramblin Twig
description: A material dropped by Bramblin or Brambleghast that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Brave Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to that of the Brave Nature, boosting Attack and lowering Speed.

name: Bread
description: An ingredient used for cooking curry at camp.

name: Briar's Book
description: A proof copy of exploration notes covering the Area Zero Underdepths, detailing events and Briar's thoughts.

name: Brick Mail
description: A piece of stationery with a tough-looking brick pattern that a Pokémon can hold to deliver a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation IV games and event-only.

name: Brick Piece
description: A valuable chunk of brick or tile that has no use other than being sold.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II games.

name: BridgeMail D
description: Stationery featuring a red drawbridge that can be held by a Pokémon to carry a written message.
notes: One of several BridgeMail variants exclusive to Generation V.

name: BridgeMail M
description: Stationery featuring a print of an arched bridge that can be held by a Pokémon to carry a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation V Mail items and designed to be readable across all languages.

name: BridgeMail S
description: Stationery featuring a sky-piercing bridge that can be held by a Pokémon to carry a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation V; prevents PC storage and Day Care use while held.

name: BridgeMail T
description: Stationery featuring a steel suspension bridge that can be held by a Pokémon to carry a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation V Mail items; messages are written using the Easy Chat system and persist only while held or stored in the Mailbox.

name: BridgeMail V
description: Stationery that allows a Pokémon to hold and deliver a written message using preset phrases.
notes: Exclusive to Generation V mail system; prevents PC storage and certain item-transfer effects while held.

name: Bright Powder
description: A held item that lowers the accuracy of moves targeting the holder.
notes: Formatted as BrightPowder prior to Generation VI.

name: Brittle Bones
description: An ingredient used for cooking curry that adds a light umami flavor when boiled.

name: Bronze Bottle
description: A decorative picnic item made of titanium that does not rust.

name: Bronze Cup
description: A decorative picnic item made of titanium that does not rust.

name: Bronzor Fragment
description: A material dropped by Bronzor or Bronzong that can be used to craft TMs or traded for Auspicious Armor.
notes: 10 can be traded for Auspicious Armor in Zapapico (Scarlet only)

name: Bruxish Tooth
description: A material dropped by Bruxish that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Bubble Mail
description: Stationery featuring a print of a blue world underwater that can be held by a Pokémon to deliver a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation IV games.

name: Bug Gem
description: A Gem that boosts the power of a Bug-type move once when held.
notes: Unobtainable as a held item from Generation VI onward outside of transfers and events.

name: Bug Memory
description: A memory disc containing Bug-type data that changes the type of Silvally and the type of its move Multi-Attack.
notes: Associated exclusively with Silvally via the RKS System; cannot be removed or given by item-manipulating effects.

name: Bug Tera Shard
description: A shard formed from shattered Tera Jewels that can be used to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type to Bug.
notes: Corresponds to the Bug type; 50 shards are required to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type.

name: Buginium Z
description: A type-specific Z-Crystal that upgrades Bug-type moves into powerful Z-Moves.
notes: Z-Crystals cannot be removed by item-negating or item-manipulating effects.

name: Bugwort
description: A wildflower found across the Hisui region with medicinal properties so bitter that wild Pokémon will not eat it.
notes: Crafting material in Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

name: Buizel Fur
description: A material dropped by Buizel or Floatzel that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Bulbasaur Candy
description: A species-based candy usable by Bulbasaur and its evolutions.

name: Burn Drive
description: A cassette to be held by Genesect that changes Techno Blast into a Fire-type move.
notes: One of the Drives associated exclusively with Genesect.

name: Burn Heal
description: A spray-type medicine that cures a Pokémon of a burn.

name: Burnt Berry
description: A Berry that cures a Pokémon of freeze when used or when held.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II; succeeded by the Aspear Berry from Generation III onward.

name: Butter
description: A cooking ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: B&W Grass Chairs
description: A set of chairs designed for picnicking, inspired by the B&W Grass Tablecloth.

name: B&W Grass Tablecloth
description: A decorative picnic tablecloth with a black-and-white grass-themed design.
notes: A picnicker on Reveler's Road in front of the Kitakami Hall will give the player the B&W Grass Chairs if this item is in their possession.

name: Cacnea Needle
description: A material dropped by Cacnea or Cacturne that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Cake-Lure Base
description: A type of field provision that enhances the flavor of other foods it is mixed with.

name: Calcium
description: A vitamin drink that increases a Pokémon’s Special Attack.

name: Calm Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to that of the Calm Nature.

name: Cameruptite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Camerupt to Mega Evolve into Mega Camerupt when held.

name: Camping Gear
description: A set of equipment that allows the player to set up a Pokémon Camp.

name: Canari Bread
description: A bun made to look like Canari's face that restores 100 HP to a Pokémon when used.
notes: Introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

name: Candy Jar
description: Contains all candy, including Rare Candies.

name: Candy Truffle
description: A sweet-fleshed truffle packed full of mysterious energy that is used as a crafting material.

name: Capsakid Seed
description: A material dropped by Capsakid or Scovillain that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Carbink Jewel
description: A material dropped by Carbink that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Carbos
description: A vitamin that increases a Pokémon’s Speed.

name: Card Key
description: A key card used to open a locked shutter in the Goldenrod Radio Tower.
notes: Johto variant used in the Goldenrod Radio Tower.

name: Card Key
description: A key card used to open locked doors inside the Silph Co. office building in Saffron City.
notes: Kanto variant used in the Silph Co. building

name: Careful Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to that of the Careful Nature.

name: Carrot Seeds
description: Seeds that can be planted in certain fields to grow a special carrot depending on the location.

name: CascadeBadge
description: A badge item internally used like Safari rocks.
notes: Index number 0x16; unobtainable.

name: Casteliacone
description: A Castelia City specialty soft-serve ice cream that heals all non-volatile status conditions and confusion of a Pokémon.

name: Caster Fern
description: A fern used for crafting items made to be thrown.

name: Catching Charm
description: A mysterious charm that increases the chance of getting a critical catch.

name: Catching Pocket
description: Contains all available varieties of Poké Ball and Berries.

name: Caterpie Candy

name: Endorsement

name: Energy Root
description: A very bitter herbal medicine that restores a Pokémon’s HP but lowers its friendship.

name: Enigma Stone

name: Enigmatic Card

name: Entei Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Entei.

name: Eon Flute

name: Eon Mail

name: Eon Ticket
description: A special ticket that allows travel to Southern Island.

name: Espurr Fur

name: Eternal Ice

name: Exp. Candy M

name: Exp. Candy XS

name: Exp. Charm

name: Explorer Kit

name: Fab Mail

name: Fairium Z

name: Fairy Feather

name: Falinks Sweat

name: Falinksite

name: Fame Checker
description: A device that records and recalls information and quotes about famous people.

name: Fancy Apple
description: A high-quality apple ingredient used primarily for cooking curry.

name: Farfetch'd Candy

name: Fashion Case

name: Fast Ball

name: Favored Mail

name: Feather Ball

name: Feebas Scales

name: Firium Z

name: Fishing Rod

name: Flame Orb

notes: Known as Muscle Wing prior to Pokémon Sword and Shield.

name: Muscle Mochi
description: A mochi cake item that increases a Pokémon’s Attack effort values.

name: Mushroom Cake
description: A cake made by combining mushrooms with a Cake-Lure Base that attracts certain Pokémon when thrown.
notes: Potently effective at attracting monstrous and dragon-like Pokémon.

name: Music Mail
description: A type of Mail that can hold a written message and be held by a Pokémon.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II games.

name: Mustard
description: A spicy condiment ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: Mysterious Balm
description: A mysterious balm used when battling Arceus.
notes: Removed from the player's satchel after completing the battle with Arceus.

name: Mysterious Shard L
description: A large mysterious shard that can be exchanged for a Slate at Ramanas Park.
notes: Introduced in Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl version 1.1.0 update.

name: Mysterious Shard S
description: A small shard that emanates an enigmatic power and can be exchanged for a Slate at Ramanas Park.
notes: Introduced in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl version 1.1.0 update.

name: MysteryBerry
description: A Berry that restores 5 PP to one of a Pokémon’s moves when used or when consumed while held.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II games; succeeded by the Leppa Berry from Generation III onward.

name: Mystery Egg
description: An unusual Egg found by the Day-Care Couple and given to Mr. Pokémon.

name: Mystic Ticket
description: An event ticket that allows access to the hidden island Navel Rock.

name: Mystic Water
description: A type-enhancing held item that boosts the power of Water-type moves.

name: Mythical Pecha Berry
description: An event-exclusive Pecha Berry of the highest quality that grants access to the Mochi Mayhem epilogue in Kitakami.
notes: Disappears from the Bag once the Mochi Mayhem epilogue has started.

name: N-Lunarizer
description: A machine that fuses Necrozma with Lunala or separates Dawn Wings Necrozma back into its constituent Pokémon.
notes: Developed by Colress as Colress Machine No. 1199 for the Ultra Recon Squad.

name: N-Solarizer

notes: Also known as Colress Machine No. 1198.

name: Nacli Salt
description: A material dropped by the Nacli evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Naive Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s nature to Naive, raising Speed and lowering Special Defense.

name: Nanab Berry
description: A pink Berry primarily used as an ingredient, with special calming effects in certain games.
notes: Has special usage in Let's Go, Pikachu!/Eevee! and Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

name: Naughty Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to Naughty, raising Attack and lowering Special Defense.

name: Necrozma Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Necrozma.
notes: Used to encounter Necrozma and obtain a location hint from Snacksworth.

name: Nest Ball
description: A Poké Ball that becomes more effective the lower the level of the wild Pokémon.

name: Net Ball
description: A Poké Ball that is more effective when attempting to catch Water- or Bug-type Pokémon.
notes: Developed in Mossdeep City.

name: Never-Melt Ice
description: A held item that boosts the power of Ice-type moves.
notes: Formatted as NeverMeltIce prior to Generation VI.

name: Nice Butter

name: Nidoran♀ Candy

name: Nidoran♂ Candy

name: Noibat Fur

name: Nomel Berry

notes: Has high sourness; used mainly for Toughness-related recipes.

name: Noodles

name: Normal Box
description: A box that can be opened from the Bag to reveal its contents.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II games; opening it yields the Silver Trophy decoration if not already owned.

name: Normal Gem

name: Normal Tera Shard
description: A shard that can be used to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type to Normal.

name: Normalium Z
description: A type-specific Z-Crystal that upgrades Normal-type moves into powerful Z-Moves.

name: Nosepass Fragment
description: A material dropped by Nosepass or Probopass that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Nugget

name: Numel Lava
description: A material dropped by Numel or Camerupt that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Nymble Claw
description: A material dropped by Nymble or Lokix that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Oak's Letter
description: A letter from Professor Oak requesting the player to go to Route 224.
notes: Event-exclusive item used to access Shaymin in Sinnoh-based games.

name: Occa Berry
description: A Berry that weakens the damage taken from a supereffective Fire-type attack when held.

name: Oceanic Slate
description: A mysterious slate that resonates with the Oceanic Room in Ramanas Park and allows a battle with Kyogre.
notes: Only available for purchase after catching Raikou, Entei, and Suicune in Brilliant Diamond or Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres in Shining Pearl.

name: Oddish Candy

name: Oddish Leaf
description: A material dropped by the Oddish evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Old Amber

name: Old Charm
description: An ancient good-luck charm made of Pokémon bones to be taken to the elder of Celestic Town.

name: Old Gateau
description: A local specialty from the Old Chateau that cures a Pokémon of all non-volatile status conditions and confusion.

name: Old Journal
description: A stab-bound journal that once had pages torn from it, with all pages collected and restored.

name: Old Letter
description: A weathered letter entrusted to the player to be delivered to a specific person.

name: Old Rod
description: A worn-out fishing rod that allows the player to fish for Pokémon in bodies of water.

name: Old Sea Map
description: An event-exclusive key item that allows travel to Faraway Island, where Mew can be encountered.

name: Pal Pad
description: A convenient notepad used to register friends and Friend Codes and keep a record of gameplay.

name: Pamtre Berry

notes: Cannot be used directly; primarily an ingredient item.

name: Paralyze Heal

name: Paras Candy

name: Parasol Pick

name: Parcel

name: Party Sparkler Pick

name: Pass

name: Pass Orb

notes: Used exclusively for Pass Powers at the Entralink.

name: Peanut Butter
description: A sweet condiment ingredient used for making sandwiches.

name: Pearl String

name: Peat Block

name: Pebble

name: Pecha Berry

name: Pep-Up Plant

name: Pepper
description: A spicy seasoning ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: Permit

name: Pewter Crunchies

name: Phanpy Nail

name: Phantump Twig

name: Photo Album
description: A nice album for storing photos taken during the adventure.
notes: Replaced by PC option.

name: Pichu Fur
description: A material dropped by Pichu, Pikachu, or Raichu that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Pickle
description: A very sour sandwich ingredient made by pickling vegetables in a spiced vinegar brine.

name: Picnic Set
description: A picnic item that allows the player to set up picnics from the menu.

name: Pidgeotite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Pidgeot to Mega Evolve into Mega Pidgeot when held.
notes: Unaffected by item-negating effects; cannot be traded to Pokémon X and Y when held in Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire.

name: Pidgey Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Pidgey, Pidgeotto, or Pidgeot.

name: Pika-Pika Pick
description: A Pikachu-themed pick used to finish sandwiches during picnics.

name: Pikachu Candy
description: A species-based candy usable by Pikachu and its evolutions.

name: Pikachu Cup
description: A decorative picnic cup themed after Pikachu with no practical gameplay use.

name: Pikanium Z
description: A Pokémon-specific Z-Crystal that allows Pikachu to upgrade Volt Tackle into the Z-Move Catastropika.

name: Pikashunium Z
description: A Pokémon-specific Z-Crystal that allows Pikachu in a cap to upgrade Thunderbolt into the Z-Move 10,000,000 Volt Thunderbolt.
notes: Only usable by Pikachu wearing a cap; cannot be removed by item-manipulating effects.

name: Pikipek Feather
description: A material dropped by the Pikipek evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Pinap Berry
description: A yellow Berry introduced in Generation III, primarily used as an ingredient and with special effects in certain games.
notes: Has special effects in Let's Go, Pikachu!/Eevee! and Legends: Arceus; also has Silver and Golden variants in Let's Go.

name: Pincurchin Spines
description: A material dropped by Pincurchin that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Pineapple

name: Pink Apricorn

name: Pink Bottle
description: A decorative bottle used during picnics with no practical gameplay effect.

name: Pink Bow

name: Pink Canari Plush Lv. 1

name: Pink Canari Plush Lv. 2

name: Pink Canari Plush Lv. 3

name: Pink Chairs

name: Pink Cup

name: Pink Nectar

name: Pink Petal

name: Pink Scarf
description: A held item that raises the holder’s Cuteness in Pokémon Contests.

name: Pink Tablecloth

name: Pinsir Candy

name: Pinsirite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Pinsir to Mega Evolve into Mega Pinsir when held.

name: Pixie Plate

name: Plaid Chairs (B)

name: Plaid Chairs (R)

name: Plaid Chairs (Y)

name: Plaid Tablecloth (B)
description: A sturdy tablecloth made of thick fabric used to decorate the player's picnic.

name: Plaid Tablecloth (R)
description: A red plaid picnic tablecloth used to decorate the player's picnic table.
notes: Having this item allows a picnicker on Reveler's Road in front of the Kitakami Hall to give the player the Plaid Chairs (R).

name: Plaid Tablecloth (Y)
description: A sturdy yellow plaid tablecloth used to decorate the player's picnic.

name: Plasma Card
description: A card key needed to enter the password inside the Plasma Frigate.

name: Plume Fossil
description: A fossil of an ancient Pokémon that lived in the sky and can be restored into Archen.
notes: Counterpart of the Cover Fossil.

name: Plump Beans
description: Large, juicy beans that can be thrown as bait to attract certain Pokémon and are used as a crafting material.

name: Plusle Fur
description: A material dropped by Plusle that can be exchanged for LP or used with the Item Printer.
notes: Not used in any TM recipes

name: Poffin Case
description: A case that allows the player to store Poffins cooked from Berries.

name: Point Card
description: A card that lists the Battle Points the player has earned.

name: Poison Barb

name: Poison Gem
description: A gem infused with poison that boosts the power of a Poison-type move once when held.
notes: Unobtainable in Generation VI onward.

name: Poison Memory

notes: Associated exclusively with Silvally and the RKS System ability.

name: Poison Tera Shard
description: A shard that can be used to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type to Poison.
notes: One of the Tera Shards; 50 are required to change Tera Type, except for Ogerpon and Terapagos.

name: Poisonium Z
description: A type-specific Z-Crystal that upgrades Poison-type moves into powerful Z-Moves when held.

name: Poké Ball

name: Poké Ball
description: A mysterious ball used in Hisui to catch wild Pokémon, crafted from natural materials.
notes: Hisuian equivalent of the standard Poké Ball with a reduced catch rate.

name: Poké Doll
description: A doll that attracts the attention of wild Pokémon, guaranteeing escape from battle.
notes: Japanese name means Clefairy Doll.

name: Poké Flute
description: A flute that plays a beautiful melody capable of waking sleeping Pokémon.
notes: In some games it is only usable via interaction with Snorlax or is not kept by the player.

name: Poké Radar
description: A tool that can search out Pokémon hiding in tall grass, with a battery that recharges as you walk.
notes: Most notable for increasing the probability of encountering Shiny Pokémon through chaining mechanics.

name: Poké Toy
description: A toy that attracts Pokémon and guarantees escape from any wild Pokémon battle.

name: Pokéblock Case
description: A case used to store Pokéblocks made with a Berry Blender.

name: Pokéblock Kit
description: A set containing a Berry Blender for making Pokéblocks and a Pokéblock Case for storing Pokéblocks.

name: Pokédex
description: An electronic encyclopedia that records and displays information about Pokémon the Trainer encounters and catches.
notes: Given to selected Trainers by regional Pokémon Professors; functionality and form vary by region and generation.

name: Pokédex
description: An encyclopedia that records information on Pokémon.
notes: Index number 0x09; replaced by menu functionality.

name: Pokémon Box Link
description: A device that allows the player to access the Pokémon storage system without needing to be at a PC.
notes: Also referred to as Pokémon Box; functionality and availability vary by game.

name: Pokéshi Doll
description: A wooden toy carved in the image of a Pokémon that can be sold to a general store.

name: Polished Mud Ball

notes: A valuable item with no practical use other than being sold.

name: Poliwag Slime

name: Polka-Dot Chairs

name: Polka-Dot Cup
description: A decorative cup used during picnics.

name: Polka-Dot Tablecloth
description: A tablecloth with a fashionable polka-dot pattern used to decorate the player's picnic.
notes: Having this item allows a picnicker on Reveler's Road in front of the Kitakami Hall to give the player the Polka-Dot Chairs.

name: Polkadot Bow

notes: Exclusive to Generation II; replaced by the Silk Scarf in Generation III.

name: Poltchageist Powder
description: A material dropped by Poltchageist or Sinistcha that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Poochyena Fang

name: Pop Pod

notes: Introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

name: Portraitmail

notes: Displays Unown A when held by any Unown form.

name: Porygon Candy

name: Porygon Fragment

name: Potato Salad
description: An ingredient used to make sandwiches during picnics.

name: Potato Tortilla

name: Potion

name: Powder Jar

name: Power Anklet

name: Power Band

name: Power Bracer

name: Power Herb

name: Power Lens
description: A held item that reduces the holder's Speed in battle while increasing the amount of Special Attack EVs gained.
notes: One of the Power items; also affects breeding by passing down Special Attack IV.

name: Power Plant Pass
description: A pass that serves as an ID card allowing access to the Kalos Power Plant.

name: Power-Up Pocket
description: Contains all Evolution stones, PP Ups, and PP Maxes

name: Power Weight
description: A held item that boosts HP EV gain after battle while reducing the holder’s Speed.
notes: One of the Power items; also affects HP IV inheritance when breeding.

name: PP Max
description: Raises the PP of a selected move to the maximum possible amount.
notes: Improved version of PP Up. Cannot be used on Sketch or moves already fully boosted.

name: PP Up
description: Raises the maximum PP of a selected move by one-fifth of its base PP.
notes: Cannot be used on Sketch or Revival Blessing; effects are lost if the move is forgotten.

name: PP Up
description: A debug version of PP Up with no effect.
notes: Index number 0x32; distinct from real PP Up.

name: Precooked Burger
description: An ingredient used for cooking curry at camp.

name: Premier Ball
description: A commemorative Poké Ball with the same catch rate as a Poké Ball.

name: Pretty Feather
description: A beautiful but ordinary feather with no practical use other than being sold.
notes: Known as Pretty Wing prior to Pokémon Sword and Shield.

name: Primarium Z
description: A Pokémon-specific Z-Crystal that allows Primarina to upgrade Sparkling Aria into the Z-Move Oceanic Operetta.

name: Prism Scale
description: A mysterious scale that allows Feebas to evolve into Milotic when traded while holding it.

name: Prison Bottle
description: A mysterious bottle used to seal away the power of Hoopa and transform it into its Unbound form.

name: Professor's Mask
description: The mask that belongs to The Masked Royal, worn by Professor Kukui for his alter ego.

name: Prof's Letter
description: A letter Professor Sycamore wrote to the player's mother explaining the request he asked of her child.

name: Prop Case
description: A case that stores Props used to dress up Pokémon for Pokémon Musicals.
notes: In Black 2 and White 2, Memory Link can prepackage Props from the linked game.

name: Prosciutto
description: A salty cured ham ingredient used for making sandwiches.

name: Protective Pads
description: A held item that protects the holder from effects triggered by making direct contact with another Pokémon.

name: Protector
description: A held item that enables Rhydon to evolve into Rhyperior under specific conditions.

name: Protein
description: A vitamin drink that raises a Pokémon’s Attack stat.
notes: Not to be confused with the Ability Protean.

name: PRZCureBerry
description: A Berry that cures a Pokémon of paralysis when used or when held.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II; replaced by the Cheri Berry from Generation III onward.

name: PSNCureBerry
description: A Berry that cures a Pokémon of poison when used or held.
notes: Exclusive to Generation II; succeeded by the Pecha Berry from Generation III onward.

name: Psychic Gem
description: A gem imbued with psychic energy that boosts the power of a Psychic-type move once when held.
notes: Unobtainable as a held item from Generation VI onward.

name: Psychic Memory
description: A memory disc that contains Psychic-type data and changes the holder's type if held by a certain species of Pokémon.
notes: Associated with Silvally and the RKS System.

name: Psychic Seed
description: A consumable held item that boosts the holder's Special Defense when Psychic Terrain is active.
notes: In Generation IX, the item returns to the holder after battle if it was used.

name: Psychic Tera Shard
description: A Tera Shard that can be collected and used to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type to Psychic.
notes: Corresponds to the Psychic type; 50 shards are required to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type at the Treasure Eatery in Medali, except for Ogerpon and Terapagos.

name: Psychium Z
description: A type-specific Z-Crystal that upgrades Psychic-type moves into powerful Z-Moves.

name: Psyduck Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Psyduck or Golduck.

name: Psyduck Down
description: A material dropped by Psyduck or Golduck that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Pumkin Berry
description: A sour Berry that cures a Pokémon of freeze when used or held.
notes: Exclusive to Generation III and obtainable only via e-Reader cards; becomes an Enigma Berry when transferred to Generation IV.

name: Punching Glove
description: A protective glove that boosts the power of the holder's punching moves and prevents direct contact with targets.
notes: Stacks with the Iron Fist Ability.

name: Pungent Root
description: An ingredient used for cooking curry that adds a fragrant accent to dishes.

name: Pure Incense
description: A held item that lowers wild Pokémon encounter rates and allows Chimecho to produce Chingling Eggs when breeding.
notes: Overworld effect is identical to the Cleanse Tag.

name: Purple Nectar
description: A flower nectar that changes Oricorio into its Sensu Style when used.

name: Purple Petal
description: A pressed flower petal collected during Mina's trial, meant to be gathered with six others.

name: Pyroarite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Pyroar to Mega Evolve into Mega Pyroar during battle.

name: Qualot Berry
description: A Berry that increases a Pokémon's friendship but lowers its Defense base points.
notes: Lowers Defense EVs by 10 (not below 0); behavior varies slightly by generation.

description: An unused debugging item in Generation I that allows the player to surf without a Pokémon or required Badges.
notes: Often called Surfboard by players; index number 0x07.

name: Quick Ball
description: A Poké Ball that is more effective when used at the start of a battle.

name: Quick Candy
description: A stat-based candy that increases a Pokémon's Speed AV.

name: Quick Candy L
description: A large candy that increases a Pokémon’s Speed when used on a Pokémon of sufficient level.

name: Quick Candy XL
description: A huge candy packed with energy that raises a Pokémon’s Speed when given to one at level 60 or higher.

name: Quick Claw
description: A light, sharp claw that occasionally lets the holder move first in its priority bracket.

name: Quick Powder
description: A held item that doubles the Speed stat of a Ditto holding it.
notes: Does not work when Ditto is transformed.

name: Quiet Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s nature to Quiet, boosting Special Attack while lowering Speed.

name: Qwilfish Spines
description: A material dropped by Qwilfish or Overqwil that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Rabuta Berry
description: A rare Berry primarily used as an ingredient for Pokéblocks, Poffins, and other berry-based preparations.

name: Radiant Petal
description: A single petal given by the King of Bountiful Harvests that radiates a faint light.

name: Rage Candy Bar
description: A famous Mahogany Town candy that heals or cures a Pokémon depending on the generation.
notes: In Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, it is classified as a Key Item.

name: Raichunite X
description: A Mega Stone that allows a Kantonian Raichu holding it to Mega Evolve into Mega Raichu X during battle.
notes: Introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

name: Raichunite Y
description: A Mega Stone that allows a Kantonian Raichu holding it to Mega Evolve into Mega Raichu Y during battle.
notes: Introduced in the Mega Dimension DLC for Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

name: Raikou Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Raikou.
notes: One of the treats obtained from Snacksworth used to encounter Legendary Pokémon in Paldea.

name: RainbowBadge
description: A badge item with no programmed effect.
notes: Index number 0x18.

name: Rainbow Feather
description: A mystical rainbow-colored feather associated with Ho-Oh that allows access to the Bell Tower and the encounter with Ho-Oh.
notes: Known as Rainbow Wing prior to Pokémon Scarlet and Violet.

name: Rainbow Flower
description: A flower made from petals given by island captains that serves as proof of the player's recognized growth and initiates the final part of Mina's trial.

name: Rainbow Pass
description: A pass that allows ferry travel between Vermilion City and the Sevii Islands.
notes: One of the Sevii Island passes; required to access additional islands beyond Three Island.

name: Rainbow Slate
description: A mysterious slate overflowing with enigmatic energy that resonates with the Rainbow Room at Ramanas Park.
notes: Only available for purchase after catching Raikou, Entei, and Suicune.

name: Ralts Dust
description: A material dropped by the Ralts evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Rare Bone
description: A rare and extremely valuable bone that is prized for Pokémon archaeology and can be sold for a high price.

name: Rare Candy
description: A candy that raises a Pokémon's level by one.

name: Rash Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s Nature to Rash, raising Special Attack and lowering Special Defense.

name: Rattata Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Rattata or Raticate, including Alolan forms.

name: Rawst Berry
description: A Berry that cures a Pokémon of a burn when used or held.
notes: Spiritual successor to the Ice Berry from Generation II.

name: Rayquaza Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Rayquaza.
notes: One of the Snacksworth treats used to encounter Legendary Pokémon in Paldea.

name: Razor Claw
description: A sharply hooked claw to be held by a Pokémon that boosts critical-hit ratio and can trigger certain evolutions.

name: Razor Fang
description: A sharply hooked fang that may cause targets to flinch and can evolve certain Pokémon.

name: Razz Berry
description: A red Berry introduced in Generation III that is primarily used as an ingredient and, in some games, makes Pokémon easier to catch or restores HP.
notes: Has special direct-use effects in Let's Go, Pikachu!/Eevee! and Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

name: Reaper Cloth
description: A mysterious cloth imbued with strong spiritual energy that allows certain Pokémon to evolve.
notes: Evolves Dusclops into Dusknoir; in Legends: Arceus it is used directly instead of being held.

name: Red Apricorn
description: A red fruit used to craft Level Balls or blend into Aprijuice.

name: Red Bell Pepper
description: A sliced red bell pepper ingredient used for making sandwiches.

name: Red Canari Plush Lv. 1
description: A plush doll of Canari that holds a red charm and slightly increases the Exp. Points Pokémon gain.

name: Red Canari Plush Lv. 2
description: A plush doll of Canari that holds a red charm and increases the Exp. Points Pokémon gain.

name: Red Canari Plush Lv. 3
description: A plush doll of Canari that holds a red charm and greatly increases the Exp. Points Pokémon gain.

name: Red Card
description: A consumable held item that forces an attacking Pokémon to switch out when the holder is hit by a damaging move.

name: Red Chain
description: A mythical chain said to bind the Legendary Pokémon responsible for the creation of a region.
notes: Exists as a dummied-out Key Item in several games and is not legitimately obtainable outside Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

name: Red Dish
description: A decorative dish used during picnics.
notes: Currently unobtainable.

name: Red-Flag Pick
description: A picnic pick that flies a red flag and is used to complete a sandwich during a picnic.

name: Red Flute
description: A red glass flute whose melody snaps a Pokémon out of infatuation.
notes: One of the flutes; in some generations it serves only as a sellable item.

name: Red Nectar
description: A flower nectar that changes the form of certain species of Pokémon.
notes: Associated with Oricorio; changes it to Baile Style.

name: Red Onion
description: A cooking ingredient used when making sandwiches.

name: Red Orb
description: A legendary red orb associated with Groudon that can trigger its Primal Reversion.

name: Red Petal
description: A pressed flower petal collected during Mina's trial, one of seven different petals needed to create a Rainbow Flower.

name: Red Poké Ball Pick
description: A picnic pick used to complete sandwiches, featuring a simple red Poké Ball design.

name: Red Scale
description: A scale from the red Gyarados.

name: Red Scarf
description: A held item that raises the holder’s Coolness in Pokémon Contests.

name: Red Shard
description: A small red shard that appears to be a fragment of an ancient implement.
notes: One of the Shards.

name: Reins of Unity
description: A set of reins that allow Calyrex to unite with or separate from its beloved steed.

name: Relaxed Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon’s nature to Relaxed, raising Defense and lowering Speed.

name: Relic Band
description: A valuable bracelet from an ancient civilization that serves no purpose other than being sold.

name: Relic Copper
description: A valuable ancient copper coin that serves no purpose other than being sold.

name: Relic Crown
description: A valuable crown made by an ancient civilization that serves no purpose other than being sold.

name: Relic Gold
description: A valuable ancient gold coin with no practical use other than being sold.

name: Relic Silver
description: A valuable silver coin from an ancient civilization that is primarily meant to be sold.

name: Relic Statue
description: A valuable stone figurine from an ancient civilization that is prized by collectors.

name: Relic Vase
description: A valuable ancient vase that serves no purpose other than being sold.

name: Rellor Mud
description: A material dropped by Rellor or Rabsca that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Remedy
description: An herbal medicine that restores 60 HP to a Pokémon but lowers its friendship.
notes: Herbal medicine counterpart of the Potion.

name: Repeat Ball
description: A Poké Ball that works better on Pokémon already registered as caught.

name: Repel
description: An aerosol spray that prevents low-level wild Pokémon from appearing for a limited number of steps.

name: Reply Mail
description: Stationery designed for writing a reply that can be held by a Pokémon to deliver a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation V core series games.

name: Reset Urge
description: A Wonder Launcher-exclusive battle item that eliminates all stat changes of an ally Pokémon.
notes: Wonder Launcher exclusive. Costs 9 points to use.

name: Reshiram Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Reshiram that allows the player to encounter it.
notes: One of the treats obtained from Snacksworth used to encounter Legendary Pokémon in Paldea.

name: Resist Feather
description: A feather that slightly increases a Pokémon’s Defense base points.
notes: Known as Resist Wing prior to Pokémon Sword and Shield.

name: Resist Mochi
description: A mochi cake that increases a Pokémon's Defense base points.

name: Retro Mail
description: A piece of Mail that can hold a written message and be carried by a Pokémon.
notes: Exclusive to Generation III games.

name: Reveal Glass
description: A mysterious looking glass that allows certain Pokémon to change between their Incarnate and Therian Formes.

name: Revitalizing Twig
description: A small twig beloved by Fennekin that can soothe and cheer when chewed.

name: Revival Herb
description: A very bitter medicinal herb that revives a fainted Pokémon.
notes: Lowers friendship when used; in Ruby and Sapphire only, restores half HP instead of full.

name: Revive
description: A medicine that revives a fainted Pokémon and restores half of its maximum HP.
notes: Max Revive is a stronger version of this item.

name: Rhyhorn Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Rhyhorn or Rhydon.

name: Rhyhorn Fang
description: A material dropped by the Rhyhorn evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Ribbon Sweet
description: A ribbon-shaped sweet that can be held by Milcery to trigger its evolution.

name: Rice
description: An ingredient with a touch of sweetness used for making sandwiches.

name: Rich Mulch
description: A type of mulch used in Berry fields that can increase the yield of harvested Berries.

name: Ride Pager
description: A device that allows the player to summon registered Ride Pokémon to perform various field actions.
notes: Developed by Ilima; unobtainable as a normal item outside scripted acquisition.

name: Riding Wear
description: A special outfit automatically worn by the player while riding a Ride Pokémon.
notes: Appearance differs between Sun and Moon and Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon.

name: Rindo Berry
description: A Berry that lessens the damage taken from a supereffective Grass-type attack when held.

name: Ring Target
description: A held item that removes the holder’s type immunities to attacking moves.

name: Riolu Fur
description: A material dropped by Riolu or Lucario that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Rock Gem
description: A Gem that boosts the power of a Rock-type move once and is then consumed.
notes: Unobtainable in Generation VI onward outside of transfers.

name: Rock Incense
description: A held incense that boosts the power of Rock-type moves and affects breeding outcomes.
notes: Prior to Generation IX, it allowed Sudowoodo to produce Bonsly Eggs.

name: Rock Memory
description: A memory disc that contains Rock-type data and changes the holder’s type if held by a certain Pokémon.
notes: Associated with Silvally and its RKS System; cannot be removed or swapped by item-manipulating effects.

name: Rock Tera Shard
description: A Tera Shard that corresponds to the Rock type and can be used to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type.
notes: Requires 50 shards to change a Pokémon’s Tera Type at the Treasure Eatery in Medali; cannot be used on Ogerpon or Terapagos.

name: Rockium Z
description: A type-specific Z-Crystal that upgrades Rock-type moves into powerful Z-Moves.
notes: Unaffected by item-negating effects; cannot be removed by Trick or Fling.

name: Rockruff Rock
description: A material dropped by Rockruff or Lycanroc that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Rocky Helmet
description: A held item that damages opposing Pokémon that make contact with the holder.

name: Roller Skates
description: A pair of skates that allow the player to move faster than running and perform tricks while navigating with the Circle Pad.

name: Rolycoly Coal
description: A material dropped by the Rolycoly evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Rookidee Feather
description: A material dropped by the Rookidee evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Room Service
description: A consumable held item that lowers the holder's Speed by one stage when Trick Room takes effect.

name: Root Fossil
description: A fossil from a prehistoric Pokémon that once lived in the sea and can be regenerated into Lileep.
notes: Key Item only in Generation III; from Generation IV onward it is a normal item.

name: Rose Incense
description: An exotic-smelling incense that boosts the power of Grass-type moves and affects breeding.

name: Roseli Berry
description: If held by a Pokémon, this Berry lessens the damage taken from one supereffective Fairy-type attack.

name: Roto Bargain
description: Reduces prices at most shops by half for a limited time.

name: Roto Boost
description: Raises all stats of the user's battling Pokémon.

name: Roto Catch
description: Greatly increases the chance of catching Pokémon.

name: Roto Encounter
description: Greatly increases encounters with high-level wild Pokémon for a time.

name: Roto Exp. Points
description: Slightly increases the Exp. Points gained after battles.

name: Roto Friendship
description: Helps Pokémon in the party become friendly faster.

name: Roto Hatch
description: Helps Eggs hatch faster.

name: Roto HP Restore
description: Fully restores the HP of the battling Pokémon.

name: Roto PP Restore
description: Fully restores the PP of the battling Pokémon.

name: Roto Prize Money
description: Triples the prize money received after battles.

name: Roto Stealth
description: Prevents wild Pokémon encounters for a limited time.

name: Roto-Stick
description: A stick used to rest a Rotom Phone on that allows taking selfies from farther away.

name: Rotom Bike
description: A bicycle combined with Rotom that allows faster travel, turbo boosting, and, after upgrades, riding on water.
notes: Can be upgraded with Watts to reduce turbo recharge time; includes Water Mode and cosmetic variants in The Isle of Armor.

name: Rotom Catalog
description: A catalog of devices that Rotom like, allowing it to change between its various appliance forms.

name: Rotom Phone
description: A smartphone possessed by a Rotom that runs various apps such as the Pokédex and serves as the player’s main interface.

name: Rotom Pokédex
description: A special Pokédex device possessed by a Rotom that can speak and provide guidance, maps, and other functions.
notes: Referred to as Rotom Dex in-game; given by Professor Kukui.

name: Rotom Sparks
description: A material dropped by Rotom that can be exchanged for LP or used with the Item Printer.
notes: Not used in any TM recipes

name: Rowap Berry
description: A Berry that damages an attacker when the holder is hit by a special move.

name: RSVP Mail
description: Stationery designed for invitations that can be held by a Pokémon to deliver a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation V as a Mail item; prevents certain moves like Fling, Trick, and Switcheroo while held.

name: Ruby
description: An exquisitely beautiful, red-glowing gem that symbolizes passion and is used to repair the Pokémon Network Machine.

name: Rufflet Feather
description: A material dropped by Rufflet or Braviary that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Rule Book
description: Lists the rules for holding battles.

name: Rusted Shield
description: A legendary artifact associated with Zamazenta that allows it to assume its Crowned Shield form.

name: Rusted Sword
description: A legendary sword associated with Zacian that allows it to assume its Crowned Sword form in battle.

name: Sablenite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Sableye to Mega Evolve into Mega Sableye when held.

name: Sableye Gem
description: A material dropped by Sableye that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sachet
description: A sachet filled with fragrant perfumes that are just slightly overwhelming and loved by a certain Pokémon.

name: Sacred Ash
description: A rare ash that revives all fainted Pokémon in the party and fully restores their HP.
notes: Commonly associated with Ho-Oh

name: Safari Ball
description: A Poké Ball originally designed for use in Safari Zones.
notes: Prior to Generation VIII, usable only in Safari Zones.

name: Safety Goggles
description: A held item that protects the holder from weather-related damage and from the effects of powder and spore moves.

name: Sail Fossil
description: A fossil from a prehistoric Pokémon that once lived on land, bearing the impression of a skin sail.
notes: Counterpart of the Jaw Fossil; can be regenerated into Amaura.

name: Salac Berry
description: A Berry that raises the holder’s Speed when it is in a pinch.

name: Salad Mix
description: An assortment of vegetables used as an ingredient for cooking curry at camp.

name: Salamencite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Salamence to Mega Evolve into Mega Salamence when held.
notes: Unaffected by item-negating effects; cannot be removed from Salamence by item-manipulating moves.

name: Salandit Gas
description: A material dropped by Salandit or Salazzle that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Salt
description: A very salty seasoning used as an ingredient when making sandwiches.

name: Salt Cake
description: A cake made by combining salt with a Cake-Lure Base that attracts Pokémon resembling grass, plants, or minerals.

name: Salty Herba Mystica
description: A legendary condiment used as an ingredient for making sandwiches.
notes: One of the five Herba Mystica.

name: Sand Radish
description: A bitter root vegetable originally native to sandy beaches, used as an ingredient for crafting Twice-Spiced Radishes.

name: Sandile Claw
description: A material dropped by the Sandile evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sandshrew Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Sandshrew or Sandslash, including Alolan forms.

name: Sandshrew Claw
description: A material dropped by Sandshrew or Sandslash that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sandwich
description: A dish made by sandwiching vegetables, meat, or other ingredients between two pieces of bread, often enjoyed during picnics.

name: Sandygast Sand
description: A material dropped by Sandygast or Palossand that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sapphire
description: A brilliant blue gemstone used to restore the Network Machine connection to the Hoenn region.

name: Sassy Mint
description: A mint that changes the effect of a Pokémon's Nature to that of the Sassy Nature.

name: Sausages
description: An ingredient used for cooking curry at camp.

name: Scanner
description: A device found inside abandoned or submerged facilities that can be exchanged with Captain Stern for special items.

name: Scarlet Book
description: A record of an expedition into the Great Crater of Paldea written by Heath, bearing the name Sada in clumsy handwriting.
notes: Exclusive to Pokémon Scarlet; counterpart is the Violet Book.

name: Scatter Bang
description: A throwable item that creates a loud noise to scare certain wild Pokémon away.

name: Scatterbug Powder
description: A material dropped by Scatterbug, Spewpa, or Vivillon that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sceptilite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Sceptile to Mega Evolve into Mega Sceptile when held.
notes: Unaffected by item-negating effects; cannot be removed or exchanged by item-manipulating moves.

name: Scizorite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Scizor to Mega Evolve into Mega Scizor when held.

name: Scolipite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Scolipede to Mega Evolve during battle when held.

name: Scope Lens
description: A held item that raises the holder’s critical hit ratio.

name: Scovillainite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Scovillain to Mega Evolve during battle.

name: Scraftinite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Scrafty to Mega Evolve during battle.

name: Scraggy Sweat
description: A material dropped by Scraggy or Scrafty that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Scroll of Darkness
description: A peculiar scroll that allows Kubfu to evolve into Single Strike Style Urshifu by revealing the secrets of the path of darkness.
notes: Counterpart is the Scroll of Waters.

name: Scroll of Waters
description: A peculiar scroll that allows Kubfu to evolve into Rapid Strike Style Urshifu.
notes: Counterpart to the Scroll of Darkness.

name: Scyther Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Scyther.

name: Scyther Claw
description: A material dropped by Scyther, Scizor, or Kleavor that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sea Incense
description: A held incense that boosts the power of Water-type moves and affects Azurill breeding.
notes: Prior to Generation IX, it allowed Marill and Azumarill to produce Azurill Eggs.

name: Seal Bag
description: A tiny bag that can hold ten Seals for decorating Poké Balls.
notes: Apparently replaced by the Seal Case.

name: Secret Key
description: A key item that unlocks the front door of the Cinnabar Island Gym.
notes: Kanto variant used to access the original Cinnabar Gym.

name: Secret Key
description: A high-tech key that emits a special electronic signal to open a door at a specific location.
notes: Distinct from the Kanto Secret Key; used to access Rotom’s Room in Eterna City.

name: Secret Medicine
description: A fantastic medicine that fully heals a Pokémon and is used to resolve certain story events.
notes: Known as Secret Potion in English prior to Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl.

name: Seed of Mastery
description: A rare seed that can be exchanged to upgrade a Pokémon’s moves, allowing advanced techniques depending on the game.
notes: Treated as distinct internal items between Legends: Arceus and Legends: Z-A despite sharing name and appearance.

name: Seedot Stem
description: A material dropped by the Seedot evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Seel Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Seel or Dewgong.

name: Seel Fur
description: A material dropped by Seel or Dewgong that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sentret Fur
description: A material dropped by Sentret or Furret that can be exchanged for LP or used with the Item Printer.
notes: Not used in any TM recipes

name: Serious Mint
description: A mint that changes a Pokémon’s Nature effect so that no stat is increased or decreased.

name: Seviper Fang
description: A material dropped by Seviper that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Sewaddle Leaf
description: A material dropped by the Sewaddle evolutionary line that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Shaderoot Carrot
description: A carrot that emits a scent beloved by Spectrier, used to summon it at the Crown Shrine.

name: Shadow Mail
description: A Duskull-print Mail that can be held by a Pokémon to store a written message.
notes: Exclusive to Generation III games.

name: Shalour Sable
description: A local specialty shortbread from Shalour City that cures all non-volatile status conditions and confusion.
notes: Local specialty of Shalour City.

name: Sharp Beak
description: A held item that boosts the power of Flying-type moves.

name: Sharpedonite
description: A Mega Stone that allows Sharpedo to Mega Evolve into Mega Sharpedo.

name: Shed Shell
description: A discarded carapace that allows the holder to switch out of battle regardless of trapping effects.

name: Shell Bell
description: A held item that restores a little HP to the holder every time it inflicts damage.
notes: Made from Shoal Salts and Shoal Shells.

name: Shellder Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Shellder or Cloyster.

name: Shellder Pearl
description: A material dropped by Shellder or Cloyster that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Shellos Mucus
description: A material dropped by Shellos or Gastrodon that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

description: A decorative dish used during picnics with no practical effect.
notes: Currently unobtainable.

name: Yellow Flute
description: A yellow glass flute that snaps a Pokémon out of confusion.
notes: Serves no practical purpose in Generation V and Pokémon X and Y other than being sold.

name: Yellow Nectar
description: A flower nectar that changes the form of certain species of Pokémon.
notes: Associated with Oricorio; changes it to Pom-Pom Style when used.

name: Yellow Petal
description: A pressed yellow flower petal collected during Mina's trial to eventually create a Rainbow Flower.

name: Yellow Scarf
description: A held item that raises the holder's Toughness in Pokémon Contests.

name: Yellow Shard
description: A small yellow shard that appears to be a fragment of an implement made long ago.
notes: One of the four Shards.

name: Yellow Tablecloth
description: A simple yellow tablecloth used to decorate the player's picnic.
notes: A picnicker on Reveler's Road in front of the Kitakami Hall will give the player the Yellow Chairs if this item is in their possession.

name: Yogurt
description: A sweet and sour condiment used as an ingredient when making sandwiches.

name: Yungoos Fur
description: A material dropped by Yungoos or Gumshoos that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Z-Power Ring
description: A mysterious ring that enables Pokémon to use Z-Power and perform Z-Moves when equipped with the appropriate Z-Crystal.
notes: Replaces the original Z-Ring and can later also enable Mega Evolution after obtaining a Key Stone.

name: Z-Ring
description: A mysterious bracelet that allows a Trainer and their Pokémon to gather Z-Power and perform Z-Moves.
notes: In Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, it is superseded by the Z-Power Ring, which can use more Z-Moves.

name: Zangoose Claw
description: A material dropped by Zangoose that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Zap Plate
description: A stone tablet associated with Arceus that boosts the power of Electric-type moves.
notes: Functions as a Key Item in Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

name: Zapdos Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Zapdos.

name: Zapdos Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Zapdos.
notes: One of the legendary Pokémon treats obtained from Snacksworth and used to encounter Zapdos in Paldea.

name: Zekrom Treat
description: A snack made from ingredients favored by the Legendary Pokémon Zekrom.
notes: Used to encounter the Legendary Pokémon Zekrom in Paldea and to receive hints from Snacksworth.

name: Zeraorite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Zeraora to Mega Evolve during battle when held.

name: Zinc
description: A vitamin drink that increases a Pokémon’s Special Defense base points.

name: Zoom Lens
description: A held item that boosts the holder's move accuracy when it acts after its target in the same turn.
notes: In Diamond and Pearl, the description incorrectly stated it boosted critical-hit ratio instead of accuracy.

name: Zorua Fur
description: A material dropped by Zorua or Zoroark that can be used to craft TMs at the TM Machine.

name: Zubat Candy
description: A species-specific candy that increases all AVs by 1 point for Zubat or Golbat.

name: Zygarde Cube
description: A key item that stores Zygarde Cells and Cores and allows changing Zygarde's form and abilities.

name: Zygardite
description: A mysterious Mega Stone that allows Zygarde in its Complete Forme to Mega Evolve during battle.
